topic: Vehicle title/ownership transfer fee and deadline after a private sale: NY DMV, CT DMV, Mexico City (SEMOVI/Finanzas CDMX)

findings.what: New York DMV title transfer fee (MV-82)
findings.quote: The title itself costs $50 in New York, and you pay it at the NY DMV.

findings.what: New York DMV deadline to apply for new title/registration after private sale
findings.value: 30 days (practical target); up to 180 days before late fees formally apply
findings.quote: The buyer has 30 days to apply for a new title, normally using MV-82... the buyer has 180 days to complete the transfer before late fees apply, but every day before then is a day driving without registration in their own name.

findings.what: New York additional sales tax due at title transfer (on top of the $50 title fee)
findings.quote: Beyond the $50 title fee, New York charges 4% state sales tax plus local county/city tax (total typically 7.5-8.875% depending on location).
The fee to transfer a vehicle title in CT is $25.

findings.what: Connecticut deadline to complete title transfer after private sale
findings.quote: most Connecticut title transfers must be completed within 30 days of the sale date to avoid late fees

findings.what: Connecticut late-filing penalty for missing the title-transfer deadline
findings.quote: If you don't meet that deadline, you will have to pay a fee of $50.

findings.what: Mexico City (CDMX) cambio de propietario fee, 2026
findings.quote: El costo publicado para 2026 es de 433 pesos.

findings.what: Mexico City cambio de propietario deadline after sale
findings.quote: El comprador tiene 15 días hábiles a partir de la fecha de la compraventa. The count begins on the sale date itself, not when you start the process.

findings.what: Mexico City consequence of missing the cambio de propietario deadline (no explicit fine found; liability risk instead)
findings.value: no specific fine found; vehicle remains registered to seller, who stays liable for fines/violations tied to the plate
findings.quote: The document does not specify any fine or penalty for missing the 15-business-day deadline. It only emphasizes that delaying creates problems: the vehicle remains registered to the seller, who remains liable for any fines or violations associated with the license plate.

findings.what: Variant CDMX fee figures reported by other 2026 sources (illustrates some spread)
findings.quote: some sources show slight variations, with costs of $358 or $417 pesos mentioned for 2026

notFound.what: An explicit, confirmed late-penalty peso amount for missing CDMX's 15-business-day cambio de propietario deadline (sources describe ongoing liability risk but not a specific fine figure)
